title: Merge Triplets to Form Target Triplet
pattern: Greedy: use every triplet that cannot overshoot
statement: Merging two triplets takes the **maximum** in each of the three positions. Given `triplets` and a `target` triplet, return `True` if `target` can be obtained by merging some of the triplets (any number of them, in any order).

example.why: Merging [2, 5, 3] and [1, 7, 5] gives [2, 7, 5]. The triplet [1, 8, 4] must be avoided because of its 8.

picture: Picture building the target by merging triplets, where a merge keeps the larger value in each position. A triplet with any value *above* the target's can never be used: once merged in, that too-big value could never come down again. Merge all the other triplets together, since that can only help. If the result equals the target, it can be formed.
idea: Merging only ever makes values **larger**. A triplet with any value above the target at that position would push it past the target for good — such a triplet can never be used.
Every other triplet is harmless: all its values are ≤ the target, so merging it in can never overshoot. So simply **merge all harmless triplets**.
If that merged result equals the target, the answer is `True`. Otherwise some target value is not supplied by any usable triplet → `False`.

say.1: LeetCode puts every answer inside a class named `Solution`. It is only a wrapper: the real work happens in the function below it.
say.2: The function we must write. It gets the `triplets` and the `target`, and answers whether merging some of them gives exactly the target.
say.3: The result of merging every usable triplet so far.
say.6: Is each of its three values at most the target's value in that position? Only then can it be used safely.
say.11: Merge it in: in each of the three positions keep the larger value.
say.13: Did merging all the usable triplets give exactly the target?
